subject: Service recovery readout & action matrix — availability event Nov 24
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: James Sullivan <j.sullivan@acmepay.com>, support@acmepay.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Service recovery readout & action matrix — availability event Nov 24

James / AcmePay team,

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the availability degradation you saw on Nov 24. Below is a concise executive readout (root cause, timeline highlights, immediate mitigations) and an action matrix with owners and delivery dates. We will follow this with the full technical postmortem and artefacts (attached).

Executive summary: the event was caused by a rare interaction between a recent autoscaler change and our dedicated-pool eviction logic. Under a short spike in background model garbage-collection (KV cache trimming) the autoscaler misestimated available slots, which triggered an aggressive eviction path that caused a rolling disruption to a subset of your reservation-backed workers. That rolling eviction coincided with a model rollout, amplifying token-serving latency and leading to a partial availability impact for requests routed to your dedicated pool.

What we did immediately:
- Identified and reverted the autoscaler heuristic within 18 minutes of detection (Nov 24 02:17 UTC).
- Applied a hard guard on eviction thresholds for all dedicated pools (protects pinned capacity).
- Rolled back the model rollout that increased KV pressure (completed by Nov 24 03:05 UTC).
- Re-routed a portion of traffic to a verified compatible model variant while we validated the fix.

Key timeline (attached: recovery_timeline.csv):
- 01:52 UTC — monitoring alert: elevated token queueing for your dedicated pool.
- 02:03 UTC — spike correlated with background KV cache trimming.
- 02:17 UTC — autoscaler heuristic reverted (mitigation 1).
- 02:55 UTC — confirm reduced eviction events; begin staged traffic rebalancing.
- 03:05 UTC — rollback of model rollout; full recovery validated by 03:30 UTC.

Action matrix (owners / target):
- Engineering (Grace O'Connor) — root-cause fix for autoscaler heuristic; unit + integration tests added. ETA: 2026-12-03.
- Platform (Marissa Cole) — permanent guard for dedicated-pool eviction; config flag and anomaly alerting. ETA: 2026-11-30.
- Customer success (Hannah Schmitt) — verification plan with AcmePay and timeline for evidence of completeness. ETA: 2026-12-01 (initial verification call).
- Controls (Engineering + Security) — evidence pack for audit (logs, rollbacks, reproducer). ETA: 2026-12-07.

Attachments included: postmortem-summary.pdf (summary + technical appendix), recovery_timeline.csv (detailed event log).

Next steps I propose: 30-minute verification call on Nov 30 to walk through the verification-checklist and confirm you have the telemetry you expect. Please let me know a preferred time, or I can send a calendar invite for 11/30 10:00 PT.

We sincerely apologise for the disruption. We take availability events seriously and will be transparent about progress and evidence as we execute the action matrix.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
H: 415-555-0142
redwood.ai

Attachments: recovery_timeline.csv (text/csv), postmortem-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: James Sullivan <j.sullivan@acmepay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@acmepay.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service recovery readout & action matrix — availability event Nov 24

Hannah,

Thanks for the fast readout and the attachments. A couple quick questions for us before the verification call:

1) Can you confirm whether any customer data (requests or embeddings) were dropped or lost during the eviction window? We need to confirm data integrity on our side.
2) For the verification run, what telemetry should we expect to see in our dashboards and for how long will Redwood retain the event logs? We may need them for our internal audit.
3) Given the customer impact, what is Redwood proposing in terms of customer remediation (service credit or contractual concession)?

Appreciate the transparency. We want to be sure this is fully closed and verified before sign-off.

- James
James Sullivan
Head of Platform Ops, AcmePay
j.sullivan@acmepay.com

On Wed, Nov 25, 2026 at 09:15 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> James / AcmePay team,
> 
> Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the availability degradation you saw on Nov 24....

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Service recovery readout & action matrix — AcmePay follow questions

Grace / Marissa — forwarding AcmePay's follow-up. They asked three items we need to answer before the Nov 30 verification call: data integrity confirmation, log retention window + how we will present telemetry, and remedial compensation. Proposed responses below — please edit/correct.

Proposed answers:
- Data integrity: engineering confirmed there were no accepted write-path failures for customer requests; no persisted user data was lost. Some in-flight requests saw token-level retries and a small number of 5xx responses recorded under the eviction window; we should quantify exact counts. (Owner: Grace — please attach count by 11/27.)
- Telemetry & retention: propose we provide a filtered audit bundle (request ids, timestamps, token latency histograms) covering Nov 24 00:00 — Nov 26 00:00 UTC. Retention for this bundle will be 90 days in the evidence pack; raw logs remain per standard retention. (Owner: Marissa — confirm export and retention policy.)
- Remediation: recommend a one-week pro rata service credit applied to your Dec invoice as a gesture of goodwill. If AcmePay would prefer an SLA amendment or other contractual language, we can escalate to legal. (Owner: Hannah — confirm amount and approval path.)

I attached a working verification-checklist (verification-checklist.xlsx) that we can send to the customer with the filtered bundle. If you both approve the above wording, I will send the formal reply and schedule the Nov 30 verification call.

Hannah

Attachments: verification-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: James Sullivan <j.sullivan@acmepay.com>, support@acmepay.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service recovery readout & action matrix — availability event Nov 24

James — thanks for the questions and the quick reply. Below is a concise set of commitments and the verification plan we will execute ahead of the Nov 30 call.

Commitments and verification plan:
1) Data integrity: engineering confirms no persisted customer data was lost. We will provide a filtered audit bundle containing request ids, timestamps, and outcome codes (success/5xx/retry) for Nov 24 00:00 — Nov 26 00:00 UTC. Owner: Grace O'Connor. Delivery ETA: 2026-11-29 17:00 UTC.

2) Event logs and telemetry: we will deliver a telemetry snapshot (latency histograms, KV cache pressure metrics, autoscaler events) and a short doc explaining which charts correspond to which parts of the timeline. Retention: the provided evidence bundle will be available for 90 days; full raw logs are retained per our standard policy (90 days for request logs, 365 days for security logs). Owner: Marissa Cole. Delivery ETA: 2026-11-29 17:00 UTC.

3) Compensation: Redwood will apply a one-week pro rata service credit to your December invoice. If you prefer a different form of remediation (SLA amendment or expanded monitoring retention), we can discuss on the verification call. Owner: Hannah Schmitt. Action: I'll initiate the credit request and confirm the credit amount by Nov 29.

4) Technical remediation: Grace will deliver the code fix for the autoscaler heuristic with tests; Platform will deploy the permanent eviction guard and anomaly alerts. ETA: code fix 2026-12-03, config deployment 2026-11-30.

5) Follow-up: verification call scheduled for 2026-11-30 10:00 PT (https://meet.redwood.ai/hs-acmepay-followup-2026-11-30). Agenda: short recap (5m), walk audit bundle (10m), verification checklist and sign-off criteria (10m), next steps (5m).

Attachment: customer-communication-log.txt (plain text) with the timeline and change history; verification-checklist.xlsx.

Please let me know if the above scope addresses AcmePay's questions and if the proposed remediation is acceptable. We aim for full closure and a documented verification sign-off on the Nov 30 call.

Best regards,
Hannah
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: verification-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), customer-communication-log.txt (text/plain)
